questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(2, 6, 36)

(4, 5, 60)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

​(2, 6, 36)

2 × 6 × 3 = 36

36 = 36 (LHS = RHS) 

And,

(4, 5, 60)

4 × 5 × 3 = 60

60 = 60 (LHS = RHS) 

So, checking each option one by one:

Option 1) (5, 3, 48)

5 × 3 × 3 = 48

45 ≠ 48 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2) (11, 10, 280)

11 × 10 × 3 = 280

330 ≠ 280 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3) (7, 6, 125)

7 × 6 × 3 = 125

126 ≠ 125 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4) (4, 8, 96)

4 × 8 × 3 = 96

**96 = 96 (LHS = RHS) **

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(4, 5, 11)

(8, 6, 10)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: (First Number + Third Number) / 3 = Second Number.**

For (4, 5, 11)

→ ( 4 + 11) / 3

→ (15) / 3

→ 5 = 2nd number.

And,

For (8, 6, 10)

​→ ( 8 + 10) / 3

→ (18) / 3

→ 6 = 2nd number.

**1) (9, 5, 7)**

→ (9 + 7) / 3

→ 16 / 3. This is not 5. (Incorrect)

**2) (8, 7, 6)**

→ (8 + 6) / 3

→ 14 / 3. This is not 7. (Incorrect)

**3) (10, 7, 11)**

→ (10 + 11) / 3

→ 21 / 3

**→ 7 = 2nd number.**

**4) (8, 5, 11)**

→ (8 + 11) / 3

→ 19 / 3. This is not 5. (Incorrect)

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and select the most appropriate answer

**Question:**

Five friends, P, Q, R, S and T, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Who is sitting second to the left of T?

**Statements:**

(I) S sits second to the right of P. T sits to the immediate left of P.

(II) Only one person sits between Q and R. P sits to the immediate left of R.

options.text: Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.
Data in statements I and II together are sufficient to answer the question.
Data in statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question.
Data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not.

questions.solution:

**Question:** Who is the second eldest among them?

(II) S is taller than M. S is shorter than O.

questions.solution:

N > A > M

Here, information regarding height of tress S and O is not given, therefore the tallest tree cannot be determined.

(II) S is taller than M. S is shorter than O. 

O > S > M

Here, information regarding height of tress S and O is not given, therefore the tallest tree cannot be determined.

Combined statements (I) and (II) N is taller than A. A is taller than M. S is taller than M. S is shorter than O. 

N > A > M 

Here, the tallest tree cannot be determined.

Thus, **Data in statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question. **

Hence, **"Option 3"** is the correct answer.

Five people, A, B, C, D and E, have different weights each. Who is the heaviest?

(I) A is heavier than C but lighter than D.

(II) B is not the heaviest and E is not the lightest.

options.text: Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question, while data in Statement I is not.
Both Statements I and II put together are not sufficient to answer the question.
Both Statements I and II put together (and not independently) are sufficient to answer the question.
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question, while data in Statement II is not.

questions.solution:
Given: Five people, A, B, C, D and E, have different weights each. 

**Statements:**

(I) A is heavier than C but lighter than D.

D > A > C

Here, the heaviest person cannot be determined, thus statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

(II) B is not the heaviest and E is not the lightest.

Here, the heaviest person cannot be determined, thus statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

Combining (I) and (II) A is heavier than C but lighter than D. B is not the heaviest and E is not the lightest.

Here, position of E and B cannot be determined. Therefore the heaviest person cannot be determined, thus statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

**Thus both Statements I and II put together are not sufficient to answer the question.**

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pairs of numbers.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

96, 12

184, 23
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

96, 12

96 ÷ 8 = 12

12 = 12 (LHS = RHS)

And,

184, 23

184 ÷ 8 = 23

23 = 23 (LHS = RHS)

So, checking each option one by one:

Option 1) 130, 16

130 ÷ 8 = 16

16.25 ≠ 16 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2) 144, 18

144 ÷ 8 = 18

**18 = 18 (LHS = RHS)**

Option 3) 156, 19

156 ÷ 8 = 19

19.5 ≠ 19 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4) 180, 20 

180 ÷ 8 = 20

22.5 ≠ 20 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Thus, out of all the option '144, 18' follows the same logic as given.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
